formation.title: The Birth of Ruthenia
formation.text:
Kyiv stands once more as the capital of a Ruthenian state. From the rapids of the Dnieper to the forests of Volhynia, the scattered principalities and Cossack hosts have been united under one banner. But what kind of nation shall this be? The Zaporozhian tradition calls for a warrior republic, a land where every Cossack is equal in the rada and where the sabers of the Sich guard the frontier against all comers. Yet the black earth speaks a different promise: the richest soil in Europe, capable of feeding empires. Shall Ruthenia be defined by the saber or by the plow?

This choice unlocks a destiny path in the Traditions tab.

options.text: Let the Sich Rada rule. We are warriors first!

modifiers.name: Sich Republic
modifiers.text: The Rada has spoken. Ruthenia shall be governed as the Cossack forebears intended, by the free assembly of warriors, where every man carries a saber and a vote. The Sich tradition lives.

options.text: The black earth shall be our wealth and our destiny.

modifiers.name: Breadbasket of Europe
modifiers.text: The black earth yields its bounty. From the Dnieper to the Dniester, Ruthenian grain feeds the continent, and the wealth of the harvest builds a civilization that will endure.

advances.name: Ruthenian Principalities
advances.text: The fragmented Ruthenian principalities (Halych, Volhynia, Kyiv) carry the legacy of Kyivan Rus, preserving Slavic traditions of princely governance and inter-dynastic diplomacy.

advances.name: Frontier Warriors
advances.text: On the steppe frontier, Ruthenian warriors develop the mounted fighting skills that will define Cossack military tradition for centuries.

advances.name: Black Earth
advances.text: The chernozem, black earth, of the Ruthenian steppe is the richest agricultural soil in Europe, capable of producing harvests that feed entire empires.

advances.name: Kyivan Heritage
advances.text: The spiritual legacy of the Baptism of Rus and the great churches of Kyiv endures, binding the Ruthenian lands to their Orthodox Christian identity.

advances.name: Steppe Horsemanship
advances.text: Ruthenian horsemen adopt the riding techniques of the steppe nomads, breeding hardy mounts and training light cavalry capable of ranging far across the grasslands.

advances.name: Sich Democracy
advances.text: The Zaporozhian Sich develops a military democracy unique in Europe, a republic of warriors where the general assembly elects all officers and the hetman himself.

advances.name: Chumak Routes
advances.text: The Chumaks, itinerant Cossack traders, drive their ox-drawn wagons across the steppe, carrying salt from the Crimea and grain from the interior along established trade corridors.

advances.name: Rada Tradition
advances.text: The Cossack Rada, the general military council, establishes precedents of collective decision-making that constrain even the most powerful hetmans.

advances.name: Kuren System
advances.text: The kurin, the basic Cossack company of fifty to one hundred warriors, serves as both military unit and social institution, each electing its own ataman.

advances.name: Dnipro Fisheries
advances.text:
The Dnieper and its tributaries teem with fish and waterfowl, sustaining the Cossack way of life and supporting a tradition of mead-brewing from steppe honey.

Available in: Medovarnia

advances.name: Border Militia
advances.text: The men of the frontier towns and villages take their turn at the field watch, riding out to the grave mounds above the Tatar trails. When the smoke rises, the watch gathers on foot to harry the raiders and free their captives.

advances.name: Chaika Raiders
advances.text: The chaika, a light war boat carved from a single trunk and armed with falconets, enables Cossack raiders to strike Ottoman ports across the Black Sea with devastating speed.

event.title: The Chaika Fleet
event.text: From the Dnieper rapids, a fleet of chaikas sets forth, light, fast boats carved from single tree trunks and fitted with falconets. Each carries fifty warriors trained in the art of naval ambush. These Cossack raiders have become the terror of the Black Sea, striking Ottoman ports from Trabzon to Sinop and even appearing before the walls of Istanbul itself. In 1615, eighty chaikas carrying four thousand Cossacks crossed the Black Sea and burned the suburbs of the Ottoman capital. The Sultan's admirals, commanding galleys three times the size, cannot catch these ghosts who attack at dawn and vanish by nightfall.

options.text: The Black Sea trembles at the sight of our sails!

advances.name: Black Sea Raids
advances.text: Cossack fleets of up to three hundred chaikas terrorize the Ottoman Black Sea coast, raiding from Trabzon to the suburbs of Istanbul itself.

advances.name: Tabor Warfare
advances.text: The tabor, a mobile fortress of chained wagons, allows Cossack armies to defend against superior cavalry forces by creating instant field fortifications.

advances.name: Brotherhood Schools
advances.text: Orthodox brotherhoods establish schools across Ruthenian cities, teaching literacy, theology, and classical languages to defend the faith against Catholic proselytization.

advances.name: Salt Trade
advances.text: Crimean salt, transported north by Chumak caravans, becomes a staple of Ruthenian commerce, enriching the trading towns along the Dnieper.

advances.name: Zaporozhian Fleet
advances.text: The organized naval forces of the Zaporozhian Host maintain permanent shipyards along the Dnieper, capable of launching raiding expeditions across the Black Sea.

advances.name: Khmelnytsky Uprising
advances.text: Bohdan Khmelnytsky's rebellion of 1648 shatters the old order and creates an independent Cossack Hetmanate, the first Ruthenian state in centuries.

event.title: The Khmelnytsky Uprising
event.text: The Cossack Host has risen. Under Bohdan Khmelnytsky, the Zaporozhian Cossacks have shattered the armies sent to subjugate them, winning victory after victory at Zhovti Vody, Korsun, and Pyliavtsi. The old order is broken. For the first time, a Cossack Hetmanate governs an independent state in the heart of Europe. But this triumph carries a question that will echo for generations: can the Hetmanate stand alone against the empires that surround it, or must it seek the protection of a greater power? At Pereiaslav, envoys offer an alliance that would secure borders but bind the nation's fate to another throne.

options.text: The Hetmanate shall stand on its own strength!

modifiers.name: Cossack Autonomy
modifiers.text: The Hetmanate stands independent. The Cossack Host answers to no foreign sovereign, and the rada governs as the ancient liberties demand.

options.text: Sign the Treaty. Our borders need guarantees.

modifiers.name: Pereiaslav Compact
modifiers.text: Through alliance with a great power, the Hetmanate secures its borders and gains access to resources that no frontier state could muster alone.

advances.name: Registered Cossack Army
advances.text: The system of registered Cossacks transforms irregular frontier warriors into a disciplined standing army organized into polk regiments under professional polkovnyks.

advances.name: Hetmanate Governance
advances.text: The Cossack Hetmanate develops a sophisticated administrative system with elected officials, written law codes, and a military bureaucracy.

advances.name: Mohyla Academy Tradition
advances.text: The Kyiv-Mohyla Academy, the first Orthodox institution of higher learning in the East Slavic world, trains clergy, diplomats, and scholars who shape Ruthenian intellectual life.

event.title: The Kyiv-Mohyla Academy
event.text: In 1632, Metropolitan Petro Mohyla transformed a modest brotherhood school into something unprecedented, the first Orthodox institution of higher learning in all the East Slavic lands. Taking the Jesuit colleges of Poland as his model, Mohyla created a curriculum that married Latin scholarship with Orthodox theology. The Academy's library holds eight thousand volumes, nearly all in Latin, opening a window onto Western philosophy, science, and letters that no Orthodox institution had offered before. Graduates go on to lead churches, advise hetmans, and carry learning across Eastern Europe. The question is what this learning shall serve: the defense of Orthodox tradition, or the embrace of Western innovation?

options.text: The Academy shall be a bulwark of Orthodox faith.

modifiers.name: Orthodox Scholarship
modifiers.text: The Academy becomes a fortress of Orthodox learning, training clergy and scholars who defend the faith through reason and erudition.

options.text: Let us learn from the West and surpass them.

modifiers.name: Western Learning
modifiers.text: Adopting the Jesuit method and Latin curriculum, the Academy bridges East and West, bringing European knowledge to the Orthodox world.

advances.name: Orthodox Brotherhoods
advances.text: Lay Orthodox confraternities organize schools, printing presses, and charitable works. The Dormition Brotherhood of Lviv bought the press of Ivan Fedorov and printed in Church Slavonic from 1591.

advances.name: Grain Export
advances.text:
Ruthenian grain, produced in staggering quantities from the black earth, enters European markets via the Dnieper and overland trade routes.

Available in: Chernozem Estate

advances.name: Mazepa's Golden Age
advances.text: Under Hetman Ivan Mazepa, the Hetmanate experiences an extraordinary cultural flourishing, churches, academies, and printing presses proliferate across the land.

event.title: Mazepa's Golden Age
event.text: Under Hetman Ivan Mazepa, the Hetmanate enters its golden age. A patron of extraordinary vision, Mazepa pours wealth into churches, monasteries, and the Kyiv-Mohyla Academy, where enrollment swells past two thousand students. The distinctive Ukrainian Baroque architecture, exuberant, colorful, defiant, rises across the land. The Hetmanate's courts administer justice, its printing presses publish theological and scholarly works, and its Cossack officers evolve into a cultured elite that rivals the Polish szlachta in sophistication. It is a brief, brilliant flowering of Ruthenian civilization.

advances.name: Regimental System
advances.text: The polkova systema, the regimental territorial system, organizes the Hetmanate into military-administrative districts, each providing troops and governance.

advances.name: Sloboda Settlement
advances.text: Sloboda, free settlements exempt from taxation, attract settlers to the frontier, populating empty steppe lands with farming communities.

advances.name: Cossack Constitution
advances.text: Pylyp Orlyk's Constitution of 1710, among the earliest in Europe, codifies the rights of Cossacks and limits the power of the Hetman through constitutional principles.

advances.name: Steppe Cavalry Tactics
advances.text: Evolving Cossack cavalry tactics blend steppe nomadic tradition with European military science, producing light horsemen of exceptional speed and striking power.

advances.name: National Awakening
advances.text: The Ruthenian national awakening sees poets, scholars, and historians rediscover and celebrate the distinct Ruthenian identity, language, and cultural heritage.

advances.name: Modern Agriculture
advances.text: Scientific farming methods applied to the incomparable chernozem transform Ruthenia into the breadbasket of Europe, with grain exports feeding the continent.

advances.name: Kobzar Tradition
advances.text: The kobzari, blind wandering minstrels who sing the epic dumy, preserve the memory of Cossack glory. They are bound in guilds with an elected elder, a secret speech of their own and years of apprenticeship before a singer may take the road.

advances.name: University Reform
advances.text: Building on the Mohyla Academy tradition, Ruthenian universities embrace modern scholarship, training a new generation of intellectuals and professionals.

advances.name: Haidamaka Rising
advances.text: The Haidamaka uprisings channel the Cossack martial spirit into popular revolts, demonstrating that the tradition of armed resistance endures in the Ruthenian heartland.

destiny.name: The Ruthenian Destiny
destiny.text: Ruthenia has risen from the ashes of fragmentation. With Kyiv secured and stability restored, the nation must now choose its path, the saber or the plow, conquest or cultivation.

event.title: The Ruthenian Destiny
event.text: The land of Ruthenia stands united once more. From the Carpathian foothills to the Dnieper rapids, a nation has been forged from the scattered principalities and Cossack hosts. The rada has convened, the banners have been raised, and Kyiv stands proud. What was broken by the Mongol tide has been restored. Now the question is not whether Ruthenia shall survive, but what it shall become.

destiny.name: The Black Sea Gate
destiny.text: Seize the gateway to the Black Sea. Take the Crimean port of Kaffa, secure the Zaporizhzhian rapids at Kichkas and fortify the crossing, as the first Sich was fortified, to hold the road south.

conditions.text: We own Kichkas and it has a fort, from a Stockade up

event.title: The Gate of the Black Sea
event.text: Kaffa has fallen to Cossack arms. The great slave market of the Crimea, where for centuries the Khan's raiders sold captured Ruthenians into Ottoman bondage, is ours. At Kichkas, the Zaporizhzhian rapids thunder beneath our boats. The gateway to the Black Sea stands open. The raids that terrorized our people for generations will now flow in the opposite direction.

options.text: The Crimea shall know our wrath!

destiny.name: The Crimean Conquest
destiny.text: Break the Crimean Khanate. Capture the Perekop gate, the fortress of Azov and Qirq Yer, the rock where the khans first sat, to dominate the northern Black Sea coast.

event.title: The Fall of the Crimea
event.text: The Crimean Khanate is broken. Perekop, the narrow isthmus that shielded the peninsula for centuries, has been stormed. At Azov, the fortress that guarded the Don estuary has capitulated. For the first time in memory, Ruthenian power extends to the shores of the Black Sea without the shadow of Tatar raids. The question now is what to do with this victory. Some advocate razing every fortress and driving the remnant population out, a final reckoning for centuries of slave raids. Others counsel settlement and assimilation, turning the steppe into Ruthenian farmland.

options.text: Raze the khanate, repay centuries of suffering!

modifiers.name: Vengeance of the Sich
modifiers.text: The Crimean slave markets burn. Centuries of raids repaid in a single campaign of righteous fury.

options.text: Settle the steppe, make it ours by plow and deed.

modifiers.name: Steppe Settlement
modifiers.text: The conquered steppe is colonized by Ruthenian settlers, transforming nomad pastures into ordered farmland.

destiny.name: Black Sea Empire
destiny.text: Complete the Cossack dream: master both shores of the Black Sea. Take the ports of Sinop and Trebizond, which the Cossack boats once raided, and the Taman peninsula to forge an empire of raiders and warriors.

event.title: Masters of the Black Sea
event.text: Sinop has fallen. The Ottoman port where chaika fleets once raided now flies the Ruthenian banner. On the Taman peninsula, the Kuban gateway is secured. The Black Sea, once an Ottoman lake, then a contested frontier, is now a Ruthenian domain. From the Dnieper to the Anatolian coast, Cossack-built vessels patrol waters that their grandfathers crossed as raiders. An empire of water and steppe stretches before the nation. Some urge that the fleet be unleashed to dominate every shore. Others see in these conquests the foundation of a new Pontic empire, a great power forged from the sea.

options.text: Unleash the raiders. The sea is our hunting ground!

modifiers.name: Pontic Raiders
modifiers.text: The Black Sea belongs to Cossack raiders whose assault craft strike with impunity across both shores. Few courts receive the envoys of a raiding state.

options.text: We shall build a Pontic empire to rival the ancients.

modifiers.name: Pontic Empire
modifiers.text: A new maritime empire rises on the Black Sea, forged by conquest and sustained by naval tradition.

destiny.name: The Grain Port
destiny.text: Secure the site of Khadjibey on the Black Sea coast, future gateway for Ruthenian grain to reach European markets. Build the treasury that befits a rising agrarian power.

event.title: The Port of Khadjibey
event.text: Where the Dniester empties into the Black Sea, the port of Khadjibey has been secured. This modest anchorage sits upon the richest agricultural hinterland in Europe, the black earth that stretches endlessly north and east. Already grain-laden ox-carts line the roads. Where Chumak wagons once trudged overland, ships will now carry Ruthenian wheat to hungry markets across the Mediterranean. The future is written in grain.

options.text: Our harvest shall feed the world!

destiny.name: Black Earth Wealth
destiny.text: Fill the treasury and build up Kyiv, where the Contract Fair gathers the landowners of the whole black earth each winter to sell their harvests forward.

conditions.text: We own Kyiv and its development is at least 36

event.title: The Banking Revolution
event.text: Ruthenian grain now commands premium prices in European markets, and the treasury swells with silver. The question arises: how should this wealth be managed? One faction advocates a state bank under the Hetman's authority, a centralized instrument to fund armies, build roads, and bind subject peoples through financial dependency. Another faction, the merchants of Kyiv and Lviv, argue for open markets, let traders set prices, let capital flow freely, and Ruthenia's natural wealth will attract investment from across the continent.

options.text: The state shall command the purse.

modifiers.name: State Banking
modifiers.text: The Hetman's treasury commands the flow of capital, funding expansion and binding subjects through financial power.

options.text: Free the markets. Prosperity follows liberty.

modifiers.name: Free Markets
modifiers.text: Open markets and free trade attract investment from across the continent, though the bureaucratic costs of a merchant state weigh on the court.

destiny.name: Breadbasket Empire
destiny.text: Cover the black earth with great estates, raise a city at Khadjibey and make it the grain port of the continent. The nation that feeds Europe commands Europe.

conditions.text: At least 10 of our locations have a Chernozem Estate
We own Khadjibey, it is a city and its development is at least 11

event.title: The Granary of Europe
event.text: The transformation is complete. Ruthenian grain feeds half the continent. From the exchange floors of Khadjibey and Kyiv, merchants negotiate contracts that determine whether cities prosper or starve. The black earth has proven mightier than any army, nations that once looked upon Ruthenia as a backward frontier now court its favor. The question remains: shall this agricultural supremacy serve as a bridge to the world, binding nations through the shared table? Or shall the harvest be industrialized, its profits channeled into modernization that will make Ruthenia self-sufficient in every way?

options.text: Feed the continent, bind nations to our table.

modifiers.name: Feed the Continent
modifiers.text: Ruthenian grain diplomacy binds nations to the table, though the plowman's priority leaves the army undersized.

options.text: Industrialize the harvest, forge our own future.

modifiers.name: Industrial Harvest
modifiers.text: Modernized agriculture drives self-sufficiency and expansion, though the inland focus neglects the fleet.

units.name: Zaporozhian Cossack
units.text: Light cavalry of the Zaporozhian Sich, expert raiders and horsemen who strike fast and vanish into the steppe.

units.name: Registered Cossack
units.text: Professional Cossack soldiers organized into polk regiments, combining frontier toughness with military discipline.

units.name: Cossack Light Horse
units.text: Swift mounted warriors of the Hetmanate, descendants of the steppe tradition of mobile warfare.

units.name: Field Watch
units.text: Frontier foot who keep the watch on the steppe trails. Quick to gather and quick to strike, they are not armed to stand in a battle line.

units.name: Chaika
units.text: A light war boat carved from a single tree trunk, armed with falconets and crewed by fifty Cossack raiders. Fast and shallow-drafted, ideal for river and coastal operations.

units.name: War Chaika
units.text: An improved version of the Cossack chaika, capable of sustained Black Sea operations against Ottoman shipping.

buildings.name: Sich Fortification
buildings.text: A fortified Cossack camp modeled on the legendary Zaporozhian Sich, earthworks, palisades, and barracks defending the frontier.

buildings.name: Chumak Trading Post
buildings.text: A waystation on the Chumak trade routes where ox-drawn caravans rest and exchange salt, grain, and other goods.

buildings.name: Kyiv-Mohyla Academy
buildings.text: The first Orthodox institution of higher learning in the East Slavic world, teaching Latin, philosophy, theology, and the liberal arts.

buildings.name: Chernozem Estate
buildings.text: A farming estate on the legendary black earth of the Ruthenian steppe, producing grain in quantities that astonish European visitors.

where.text: The location's raw material is Wheat

buildings.name: Tabor Encampment
buildings.text: A defensive position of chained wagons filled with earth and armed men, the Cossack answer to enemy cavalry superiority.

buildings.name: Brotherhood School
buildings.text: A school founded by an Orthodox brotherhood to teach literacy, theology, and classical languages in defense of the faith.

buildings.name: Sloboda Settlement
buildings.text: A free frontier settlement where colonists receive tax exemptions in exchange for settling and defending empty steppe lands.

buildings.name: Medovarnia
buildings.text: A honey distillery producing mead and liquor from the abundant bee products of the Ruthenian steppe and forests.

buildings.name: Brotherhood Press
buildings.text: The printing house of an Orthodox brotherhood, set beside its school. Primers, psalters and polemical tracts are printed here in Church Slavonic.

buildings.name: Kobzar Guild
buildings.text: The brotherhood of the blind singers of a district. It keeps a lamp before its icon in the parish church, judges its own members and admits apprentices to the craft.

buildings.name: Cossack Arsenal
buildings.text: A major Cossack weapons manufactory producing arms, munitions, and equipment for the armies and fleets of the Black Sea empire.

buildings.name: Grain Exchange
buildings.text: An international grain trading hall where merchants negotiate contracts that determine whether distant cities prosper or starve.

list.name: Zaporizhian Sich
list.text: The fortress-republic on the Dnipro rapids whose Sich Rada (the assembly of all Cossacks) elected the Kosh Otaman for one-year terms and supplied Khmelnytsky's army from its kurin companies. The Sich modeled a direct democracy of the Cossack rank-and-file: the otaman ruled by acclamation and could be deposed at any council. Its egalitarian custom set permanent limits on starshyna pretensions to noble status.

list.name: Polkovnyk Regimental Administration
list.text: The territorial regiments (polky) into which Bohdan Khmelnytsky organized the liberated lands after 1648. Each of the ten polky was governed by a colonel appointed by the hetman and confirmed by the regimental Cossacks; the polkovnyk commanded the regiment in war, presided over the regimental court in peace, and administered the polk's towns and villages. Military and civil authority fused in one officer made the regiment the Hetmanate's basic governing unit.

list.name: Heneralna Starshyna
list.text: The general officer staff that served as the hetman's standing cabinet from the mid-seventeenth century. It comprised the heneralnyi obozny (quartermaster), two heneralni suddi (general judges), the heneralnyi pysar (chancellor), the heneralnyi pidskarbi (treasurer), two heneralni osavuly, the bunchuzhny (mace-bearer), and the khorunzhy (standard-bearer). From Hlukhiv after 1708 the Starshyna ran the executive offices of state.

list.name: Heneralnyi Sud
list.text: The General Court of the Hetmanate, an appellate bench presided over by the two heneralni suddi from 1654 onward. It applied a layered legal order: the Lithuanian Statute of 1588 in its 1648 Polish edition for nobility and gentry-style Cossacks, Magdeburg town law in chartered cities including Kyiv, and Cossack customary law in military matters. The court rode circuit, heard mixed Cossack-Russian cases, and disciplined the regiments through the General Military Tribunal.

list.name: Kyiv-Mohyla Academy
list.text: Founded in 1632 when Metropolitan Petro Mohyla merged the Kyiv Brotherhood School with the Pechersk Lavra school on the Jesuit collegial model. After Hadiach 1658 it gained formal academic rank and trained the literate Orthodox elite of the Hetmanate. The future hetmans Vyhovsky, Samoilovych, Mazepa, and Polubotok all studied there. By Mazepa's reign enrolment exceeded two thousand, and the academy supplied scribes for every regiment.

list.name: Pacta et Constitutiones
list.text: The layered constitutional framework that defined the Hetmanate's autonomy. The Pereyaslav Articles of 1654 enumerated the rights the Cossack Host preserved under the tsar; the Treaty of Hadiach (1658) projected a Grand Duchy of Rus' as a third partner of the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth; Pylyp Orlyk's Bendery Constitution (1710) separated legislative, executive, and judicial powers under a triannual general council. Each new hetman swore to a fresh redaction: the living constitution that leashed the protector.
